title: Federal political money is visible at a different scale from political participation
source_unit: Federal Election Commission statistical summary of committee filings
geography: United States federal elections; 2025-2026 election cycle

denominator.unit: FEC-reported committee financial activity in the 15-month period

observations.method: FEC aggregation of campaign-finance reports filed by congressional candidate committees, party committees, PACs, and communication filers through March 31, 2026.
observations.uncertainty: Totals are subject to reporting, classification, rounding, amendment, and committee-coverage boundaries; the summary does not measure unreported political activity or downstream effectiveness.
observations.subgroup: Federal congressional candidate committees, party committees, PACs, and reported independent-expenditure filers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher receipts can reflect more candidates, competitive races, fundraising technology, donor concentration, or reporting composition rather than broader civic participation or greater policy influence.

related_sources.claim: FEC publishes cycle, filer-type, and coverage-period campaign-finance tables.
FEC describes the fields available for individual contribution searches, including contributor, date, amount, and recipient committee.

boundary: This record measures disclosed committee-level financial capacity. It does not measure unique donor breadth, communication exposure, persuasion, turnout, candidate victory, policy change, corruption, or democratic legitimacy.
